claims.text: The sample is a bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystal containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Ab initio molecular dynamics with explicit oxygen-impurity modeling can predict the lattice thermal conductivity at 300 K within 10% accuracy.
The proposed approach will outperform earlier analytical or computational approaches.
The proposed approach outperforms earlier approaches because it captures atomic-scale complexity and defects.
The approach is applicable from 300 to 1200 K.
The approach is applicable to bulk-crystal samples.
Oxygen impurities and lattice defects are the relevant structural mediators.
Oxygen impurities and defects influence phonon scattering.
Oxygen impurities and defects influence electron-phonon interactions.
The lattice thermal conductivity is predicted to be 12 W/(K m) at 300 K.
Prediction accuracy will improve by 10% relative to earlier approaches.
Experiments measured total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m).
Atomic-scale structural complexity, defects, and impurities may cause variation in lattice thermal conductivity and prediction accuracy.
A deviation of more than 15% between measured and predicted lattice thermal conductivity at 300 K will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims accuracy within 10%, but it is only falsified by errors greater than 15%, leaving errors between 10% and 15% inconsistent with the accuracy claim yet non-falsifying.

The predicted quantity is lattice-only conductivity, whereas the numerical baseline is total conductivity and the mechanism invokes electron-phonon interactions. These fields do not maintain a clean lattice-versus-electronic separation.

Applicability is claimed over 300–1200 K, but the quantitative prediction and decisive lattice-conductivity test are specified only at 300 K; the proposed high-temperature total-conductivity measurement does not directly test the lattice-only prediction.
